mcqs.question: Which of the following liquids will NOT conduct electric current?

options.A: Salt water (a solution of common salt)

mcqs.explanation: Pure distilled water contains virtually no free ions, so it does not allow the flow of electric charge. The other liquids all contain dissolved ions (Na⁺, Cl⁻ in salt water; H⁺, citrate ions in lemon juice; H⁺, acetate ions in vinegar) which make them conductive. Hence option B is the correct non‑conducting liquid.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the role of dissolved substances in conductivity
mcqs.question: Why does a solution of table salt (NaCl) in water conduct electricity, while a solution of sugar (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) in water does not?

options.A: Sugar molecules dissociate into ions, but salt does not
options.B: Salt dissociates into ions that can move freely, whereas sugar molecules remain intact
options.C: Both salt and sugar dissociate into ions, but only salt ions are mobile
options.D: Neither salt nor sugar dissociate, but salt conducts because of its colour

mcqs.answer: Salt dissociates into ions that can move freely, whereas sugar molecules remain intact
mcqs.explanation: When NaCl dissolves, it separates into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, which are charge carriers and allow electric current to pass. Sugar molecules do not ionize; they stay as neutral molecules, so they cannot carry charge. Therefore option B correctly explains the difference.

mcqs.learning_point: Use simple circuits to test conductivity
mcqs.question: A student connects a simple circuit with a bulb to two separate beakers, one containing a salt‑water solution and the other containing a sugar‑water solution. In which beaker will the bulb glow brighter?

options.A: The beaker with the salt‑water solution
options.B: The beaker with the sugar‑water solution
options.C: Both beakers will make the bulb glow equally bright
options.D: The bulb will not glow in either beaker

mcqs.answer: The beaker with the salt‑water solution
mcqs.explanation: The salt‑water solution contains free ions that provide a low‑resistance path, allowing more current to flow and making the bulb glow brighter. The sugar solution lacks ions, offering high resistance, so the bulb will be dim or off. Hence option A is correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a liquid with its ability to conduct electricity?

options.B: Lemon juice – does not conduct electricity

mcqs.explanation: A solution of NaCl dissociates into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, making it a good conductor. Distilled water lacks ions, lemon juice contains ions and therefore conducts, and cooking oil is non‑polar and does not conduct. Only option C correctly pairs a liquid with its conductive property.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that some liquids conduct electricity
mcqs.question: Which statement best describes why certain liquids can conduct electricity?

options.A: All liquids conduct electricity because water is always present
options.B: No liquid can conduct electricity under any condition
options.C: Liquids that contain dissolved ions can conduct electricity
options.D: Liquids conduct electricity only when they are heated to high temperatures

mcqs.answer: Liquids that contain dissolved ions can conduct electricity
mcqs.explanation: Electrical conductivity in liquids arises from the presence of charged particles (ions) that can move freely. Pure water or non‑ionic liquids lack these carriers, while solutions like salt water have ions and conduct. Option C captures this principle.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a conducting liquid?
mcqs.explanation: Salt water contains Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that allow electric current to pass, making it conductive. Distilled water, olive oil, and ethanol lack free ions and are poor conductors. Therefore option B is the correct example.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the role of dissolved substances in conductivity
mcqs.question: What is the primary reason that a solution of copper sulfate conducts electricity?

options.A: Presence of free electrons in the solution
options.B: Presence of ions formed when copper sulfate dissolves
options.D: Large size of copper sulfate molecules

mcqs.answer: Presence of ions formed when copper sulfate dissolves
mcqs.explanation: When CuSO₄ dissolves, it dissociates into Cu²⁺ and SO₄²⁻ ions. These charged particles move under an electric field, allowing current flow. Free electrons are not present in aqueous solutions, and temperature or molecular size are not the main factors. Hence option B is correct.

mcqs.learning_point: Use simple circuits to test conductivity
mcqs.question: To test whether a liquid conducts electricity using a simple circuit with a bulb, which step should be performed first?

options.A: Connect the bulb directly to the battery without any liquid
options.B: Place two electrodes in the liquid and complete the circuit through the bulb
options.C: Heat the liquid to its boiling point before connecting the circuit
options.D: Add sugar to the liquid to increase its conductivity

mcqs.answer: Place two electrodes in the liquid and complete the circuit through the bulb
mcqs.explanation: The first action in a conductivity test is to insert two conductive electrodes into the liquid and close the circuit so that any current can pass through the bulb. This arrangement will show whether the liquid allows charge flow. The other options either bypass the liquid or introduce unrelated actions. Thus option B is correct.
